description: OWASP WebGoat (Java, Spring Boot): every deliberately exploitable lesson/challenge sink described by the lesson documentation (adoc pages, hints, code comments), labeled at the dangerous statement.

vulnerabilities.description: The raw SQL string from request parameter 'query' is executed directly with Statement.executeQuery.
vulnerabilities.note: SqlInjection_introduction_content1.adoc (What is SQL? - assignment runs user-supplied SQL)

vulnerabilities.description: The raw SQL string from request parameter 'query' is executed directly with Statement.executeUpdate.
The raw SQL string from request parameter 'query' is executed directly with Statement.executeUpdate (DDL).
The raw SQL string from request parameter 'query' (GRANT statement) is executed directly.
account/operator/injection parameters are concatenated into a string literal of a SELECT on user_data and executed with Statement.executeQuery.
vulnerabilities.note: SqlInjection_introduction_content11.adoc (Try It! String SQL injection, 'or 1=1'), code EXPLANATION constant

vulnerabilities.description: userid is concatenated (numeric context) into the query passed to prepareStatement, so only login_count is parameterized.
name and auth_tan are concatenated into a SELECT on employees and executed, allowing confidentiality compromise.
vulnerabilities.note: SqlInjection_introduction_content8.adoc (Compromising confidentiality with String SQL injection)

vulnerabilities.description: name and auth_tan are concatenated into a query executed with Statement.execute, allowing stacked UPDATE queries.
action_string is concatenated into a LIKE clause on access_log and executed, allowing stacked DROP TABLE.
userid_6a is concatenated into a SELECT on user_data (built at line 54) and executed, enabling UNION/stacked extraction of user_system_data.
vulnerabilities.note: SqlInjection_content6a.adoc (advanced, UNION), answer comment at lines 46-47

vulnerabilities.description: username_reg is concatenated into the user-exists check query and executed, a blind boolean SQL injection.
vulnerabilities.note: SqlInjection_challenge.adoc (log in as Tom; blind injection in registration)

vulnerabilities.description: The 'column' request parameter is concatenated into the ORDER BY clause of a prepared statement.
vulnerabilities.note: SqlInjection_content13.adoc / SqlInjection_order_by.adoc (ORDER BY injection to get the webgoat-prd IP)

vulnerabilities.description: Input validation that only rejects spaces is bypassable (e.g. comments), and the value reaches the concatenated query of lesson 6a.
vulnerabilities.note: SqlInjection_content12a.adoc (input validation alone is not enough)

vulnerabilities.description: Single-pass removal of SELECT/FROM plus a space check is bypassable, and the value reaches the concatenated query of lesson 6a.
The JWT 'kid' header is concatenated into a SELECT on jwt_keys, so an attacker controls the HMAC signing key.
username_login and password_login are concatenated into the login query, allowing login as Larry without the password.
Command strings built from user input are executed through '/bin/sh -c' or 'cmd.exe /c', so shell metacharacters are interpreted.
vulnerabilities.note: CommandInjection_Intro.adoc / CommandInjection_Safety.adoc (shared shell execution sink for tasks 2-4)

vulnerabilities.description: The 'base' and 'payload' request parameters are joined into a shell command and executed, leaking the WEBGOAT_BUILD_TOKEN environment variable.
The search 'title' is concatenated into a grep/findstr command (buildCommand line 108) and run through the shell, allowing the flag file to be read.
A denylist that only strips ';', '&&' and '|' is bypassable (e.g. newline, $(), backticks), and the title is executed through the shell.
readObject of the deserialization gadget passes the attacker-controlled taskAction to Runtime.exec.
The username is written unneutralized into the simulated log output, so CRLF/HTML lets an attacker forge an 'admin' log entry.
The credit card field1 parameter is concatenated unescaped into the HTML output that is rendered in the page (reflected XSS).
The 'test/:param' route value from the URL fragment is inserted with jQuery .html(), a DOM-based XSS sink.
vulnerabilities.note: CrossSiteScripting_content6a.adoc / CrossSiteScripting_content6b.adoc (DOM-based XSS, start.mvc#test/ route; comments in DOMCrossSiteScripting.java)

vulnerabilities.description: Stored comment text returned by /CrossSiteScriptingStored/stored-xss is placed into an HTML template and appended to the DOM unescaped.
vulnerabilities.note: CrossSiteScripting_content7.adoc / CrossSiteScriptingStored_plan.adoc (stored XSS assignment; StoredXssComments stores comment text unsanitized)

vulnerabilities.description: The user-supplied fullName is used as the file name under the upload directory, so '../' writes the file elsewhere.
The 'fix' removes '../' only once, so '....//' still traverses out of the upload directory.
The multipart original file name (attacker-controlled) is used as the destination name, allowing traversal.
The 'id' parameter builds a File path; the raw query-string check is bypassed with URL encoding, so files outside the cats directory are read.
Zip entry names are used unvalidated as extraction paths (Zip Slip), so entries with '../' overwrite arbitrary files.
Comment XML is parsed with a default XMLInputFactory/JAXB unmarshaller (securityEnabled=false), so external entities are resolved.
vulnerabilities.note: XXE_simple.adoc (SimpleXXE calls parseXml(commentStr, false)); 'TODO fix me disabled' comment

vulnerabilities.description: When the Content-Type is switched to XML the JSON endpoint parses the body with the XXE-vulnerable parser.
The comment body is parsed with the XXE-vulnerable parser, allowing blind out-of-band exfiltration of secret.txt via parameter entities.
The feed importer's DocumentBuilderFactory explicitly enables external general entities, which the entity resolver fetches.
vulnerabilities.note: Challenge 2 (Partner feed recovery) hints challenge2.chain.hint1/hint3 in i18n WebGoatLabels.properties

vulnerabilities.description: The base64 'token' parameter is deserialized with ObjectInputStream.readObject without any class filtering.
User XML is deserialized with XStream.fromXML without a type allowlist, allowing arbitrary object/gadget instantiation (CVE-2013-7285 style).
vulnerabilities.note: VulnerableComponents_content5a.adoc (Exploiting CVE-2013-7285 XStream); code comment references CVE-2013-7285

vulnerabilities.description: The server opens the client-supplied 'url' parameter with new URL(url).openStream() and returns the response.
vulnerabilities.note: SSRF_Task2.adoc (make the server fetch http://ifconfig.pro); the URL is regex-limited to that host in this training code

vulnerabilities.description: The allowed source is checked only for the starting URL; redirect targets are followed unchecked, so the importer reaches the internal diagnostics endpoint.
vulnerabilities.note: Challenge 2 hints challenge2.chain.hint2/hint3; code comment 'Redirect targets intentionally bypass that check'

vulnerabilities.description: The 'url' parameter is used unvalidated in a 'redirect:' view name.
vulnerabilities.note: OpenRedirect_Explained.adoc; code comment 'Intentionally vulnerable: no validation'

vulnerabilities.description: The publisher /northstar/go endpoint redirects to any 'url' parameter, which is chained into the SSRF.
vulnerabilities.note: Challenge 2 hint challenge2.chain.hint2 (look closely at the publisher link)

vulnerabilities.description: Redirect-target validation only checks that the URL contains 'webgoat', so external hosts such as webgoat.evil.com pass.
The redirect target is treated as internal if it starts with http(s)://webgoat.local, so userinfo tricks ('webgoat.local@evil.com') reach an external host.
The target is validated after one URL decode but decoded a second time downstream, so double-encoded '@' changes the real host.
Any userId from the path is used to load and return that user's profile without a horizontal access-control check.
vulnerabilities.note: IDOR_viewOtherProfile.adoc; code comment about missing horizontal access control

vulnerabilities.description: A PUT to /IDOR/profile/{userId} updates another user's color and role without checking authorization.
vulnerabilities.note: IDOR_editOtherProfile.adoc; code comment 'not checking for proper authorization'

vulnerabilities.description: The JSON /access-control/users endpoint returns all users with their hashes to any authenticated user (no admin check).
Anyone can POST a new user with admin=true (also on users-admin-fix), which bypasses the admin check of the 'fixed' listing.
vulnerabilities.note: missing-function-ac-04-users-fixed.adoc (the company fixed the problem, right?)

vulnerabilities.description: Admin menu items (Users, Config) are only hidden with CSS, relying on obscurity instead of access control.
The salaries endpoint returns every employee's SSN and salary and leaves the filtering to client-side code.
The account a new credential is bound to is taken from the client-sent userHandle instead of server-side ceremony state, so a key can be registered on Jerry's account.
vulnerabilities.note: WebAuthn_registration_assignment.adoc / WebAuthn_pitfalls.adoc ('Account taken from the client')

vulnerabilities.description: Security-question checks only run if the expected parameter names are present, so renamed parameters skip verification entirely.
vulnerabilities.note: 2fa-bypass.adoc; code comment 'Can you find the flaw?'

vulnerabilities.description: Jwts.parser().parse() accepts unsigned (alg none) tokens, so a forged admin=true claim resets the votes.
The checkout endpoint parses the bearer token with parse(), accepting unsigned alg none tokens for user Tom.
vulnerabilities.note: JWT_refresh_assignment.adoc; feedback key jwt-refresh-alg-none at line 96

vulnerabilities.description: Refresh tokens are not bound to a user and expired access tokens are accepted, so Jerry's refresh token mints a new token for Tom.
vulnerabilities.note: JWT_refresh_assignment.adoc (let Tom pay for the books)

vulnerabilities.description: The verification key is fetched from the token's own 'jku' header URL, so an attacker-hosted JWKS validates a forged token.
Verb-based authentication only blocks GET, so a HEAD request to the vote endpoint votes and receives the flag header.
vulnerabilities.note: Challenge_8.adoc (Can you still vote?); code comment 'VERB Based Authentication'

vulnerabilities.description: Password recovery relies on a guessable favorite-color answer with no lockout, and unknown users get a distinct message.
vulnerabilities.note: PasswordReset_known_questions.adoc ('There is no lock-out mechanism'), PasswordReset_wrong_message.adoc

vulnerabilities.description: The password-reset e-mail link is built from the client-supplied Host header (read at line 67), so a poisoned host leaks Tom's reset token.
The issued challenge is removed from the session but never compared with clientData.challenge, so a captured assertion of Jerry can be replayed.
vulnerabilities.note: WebAuthn_authentication_assignment.adoc / WebAuthn_pitfalls.adoc; code comment 'never compared with clientData.challenge()'

vulnerabilities.description: The JWT HMAC key is a hardcoded dictionary word, so the token signature can be brute-forced and forged.
The admin password for challenge 1 is hardcoded in source (only the 1234 part is replaced by the PIN).
vulnerabilities.note: Challenge_1.adoc (the admin forgot where the password is stashed); TODO comment 'should be random generated'

vulnerabilities.description: Default admin/admin credentials are hardcoded and accepted for the staging login.
Obfuscated hardcoded credentials (CaptainJack/BlackPearl) are sent in cleartext in the login request body.
A password is hashed with unsalted MD5, which is reversible with lookup tables.
A password is hashed with a single unsalted SHA-256, which is reversible with lookup tables.
Stage 1 password records are unsalted fast SHA-256, so equal passwords share a hash and a wordlist cracks them.
Stage 2 password records are salted but still a single fast SHA-256, so a wordlist attack per record still succeeds.
The HMAC tag is compared byte by byte with an early exit, leaking the number of matching bytes through response timing.
Session IDs are an incrementing counter plus a millisecond timestamp, so other users' session cookies can be predicted.
vulnerabilities.note: HijackSession_content0.adoc; code comment 'weak id value and mechanism'

vulnerabilities.description: Reset links come from java.util.Random, seeded with the key length for admin, so the admin reset link is fixed and predictable.
vulnerabilities.note: Challenge_7.adoc (reset the password for admin); code comment 'Admin has a fix reset link'

vulnerabilities.description: The authentication cookie is only reversed/hex/base64-encoded (not signed), so a cookie for 'tom' can be forged.
vulnerabilities.note: SpoofCookie_content0.adoc; code comment 'PoC: weak encoding method'

vulnerabilities.description: The state-changing basic-get-flag POST has no anti-CSRF token and accepts cross-origin requests.
The review endpoint's 'anti-CSRF' check compares against a static hardcoded token (line 38), so forged cross-site reviews succeed.
The JSON feedback endpoint accepts a JSON body sent as text/plain from a cross-site form without any CSRF protection.
Spring Security CSRF protection is disabled globally, so the login form is open to login CSRF.
vulnerabilities.note: CSRF_Login.adoc (see if WebGoat is vulnerable to login CSRF)

vulnerabilities.description: The generated Admin password is written (base64-encoded) to the application log at startup.
A verbose error page returns a stack trace with DB credentials and the system API token.
An unauthenticated actuator/env-style endpoint exposes the internal system API key.
A reachable blog-backup application.properties discloses the password pepper, allowing the peppered hashes to be cracked.
The /challenge/7/.git endpoint serves the repository archive, revealing the reset-link generation code.
The admin PIN that completes the password is embedded into the bytes of the public logo image.
vulnerabilities.note: Challenge_1.adoc (the admin forgot where the password is stashed)

vulnerabilities.description: The coupons endpoint lists every code, including the 100% 'get_it_for_free' coupon that the UI never shows.
The checkout trusts the client-supplied Total price instead of recomputing it server-side.
vulnerabilities.note: HtmlTampering_Task.adoc (buy the TV for a lower price)

vulnerabilities.description: Authorization checks the first 'recipient' value while the transfer uses the last, so a duplicated parameter redirects the money.
